area: Nostr event id computation, JSON serialization, and signature verification
note: No signed event with a hardcoded id or sig exists anywhere in bitchat's test suite - every test there generates a fresh random identity at runtime. The ids here are therefore derived, not transcribed. Each vector carries the exact `serialized` byte string that was hashed, so the escaping rules are auditable by eye without re-running anything.

vectors.name: geohash_chat_minimal
vectors.derivation: id = SHA-256 over the compact JSON array [0, pubkey, created_at, kind, tags, content]. The `serialized` field is the exact byte string that was hashed, emitted by python json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False, separators=(',',':')), which agrees with Foundation's JSONSerialization(.withoutEscapingSlashes) - the encoder bitchat uses - on every rule that matters here: no whitespace, '/' NOT escaped, '"' and '\' escaped, \b \t \n \f \r as short escapes, other C0 controls as \u00XX, and non-ASCII emitted as raw UTF-8 rather than \u escapes.
vectors.note: Baseline kind 20000 with only the g tag.
vectors.sig_derivation: BIP-340 Schnorr over the raw 32-byte event id with aux_rand = 32 zero bytes, by the secret behind `pubkey` (identity.json/u4pru). bitchat signs with random aux, so a correct implementation will NOT reproduce these bytes - it must VERIFY them.
